character.prompt: Pixel-art sprite sheet of a small dog companion character, matching the exact style of an existing character sheet in the same game.  STYLE - Flat-shaded 2D pixel art, no hard black outline — shapes are separated by   flat color blocks and one shade of soft dark shadow per material, same as   the reference character. - Chibi/game-cute proportions: compact, slightly oversized head relative to   body, simple facial features (no fine detail at this resolution). - Side view / profile, facing RIGHT by default (the game engine flips the   sprite horizontally in code for left-facing movement, so only a right-   facing version is needed). - Clean pixels, no anti-aliasing gradients, no dithering — flat regions of   exact palette colors only, consistent with a limited retro palette.  CANVAS / GRID - 96x96 px per animation frame, transparent background. - The character silhouette should occupy roughly the bottom 40px of the   96px-tall cell and about 28px of width at rest, centered horizontally,   standing on an implied ground line near the bottom of the cell (leave a   few px of transparent margin below the feet/paws, not flush to the very   edge) — this matches how the human character is seated in her cells.  PALETTE (reuse these exact colors so the two characters read as one world; introduce 3-5 new fur/collar colors but keep this exact set for anything that should visually "match" the human character, e.g. a collar/bandana in her hair color reads as a matching accessory):   Hair/hero-color (use for a bandana or collar, not fur): #bf0b6e, #f39ec8, #f22d99   Outfit green (optional trim/collar tag): #016646, #003529   Outfit purple/plum (optional trim): #884980, #562275, #390a52, #23083b, #761479, #520345   Skin/highlight tone: #fbbea7   Shadow tones: #07191d, #020516   Rim highlight: #f0f0f8 New fur colors: your choice, but keep it to 2-3 flat tones + 1 shadow tone, same low color-count philosophy as the reference (17 total colors on her whole sheet).  SPRITE SHEET LAYOUT (pack tightly, no gaps between rows/frames, this exact row order so it can be sliced with egions):    Row 0 (y=0):     idle     — 10 fre breathing/tail                     wag/ear twitch, weight shifting slightly, calm.   Row 1 (y=96):    run      — 10 frl quadruped                     gallop cycle, ears back, low energetic stride.   Row 2 (y=192):   jump     — 7 fra crouch                     anticipation (legs bunched under body) into a leap with                     legs extended/t   Row 3 (y=288):   stumble  — 6 frames, plays once, ~10 fps — trips forward,                     nose/chest pitcall dust puff,                     ears flop — reads as "misjudged a jump, tripped".   Row 4 (y=384):   recoil   — 7 fra snaps backward                     sharply, ears pinned flat, startled/yelp pose — reads as                     "hit something"   Row 5 (y=480):   overshoot — 5 frames, plays once, ~10 fps — leans too far                     forward mid-strcts backward —                     reads as "went out of control, overcompensated".
